430.label: Top boards rush or promote the passed pawn prematurely instead of activating the king first (king-first principle), throwing away a won K+P endgame; medium blurs to minor king/rook tempo-imprecisions (wrong square, king backward, 5th vs 6th rank) that merely slow a still-winning conversion — many flagged moves are actually 0cp non-blunders.

425.label: Top: a winning-side, natural-looking reposition/king move hangs material to an overlooked tactic (fork, trapped piece, or crashing king attack); medium broadens to subtler squanderings—a missed forcing win (Qxd3+) or tempo-losing developing/castling move that merely lets the win slip without an immediate material drop.

433.label: Top boards uniformly squander a checkmate-in-one (a safe-looking move unguards the mating net); medium boards broaden to longer forced mates (mate-in-2 through mate-in-6) plus occasional non-mating tempo/material inaccuracies.

419.label: At the peak: materially-safe king/quiet moves that waste tempo or use imperfect technique in an already-won (endgame) position (~10cp slips, no material lost); at medium it blurs by magnitude and type — into missing forced wins and mates and even hanging the winning advantage outright.

431.label: Top: a knight is shoved to the rim (Nh4/Nh5) to chase the f5/f4 bishop and is simply hung to Qxh4/Qxh5 for a full piece in the opening; medium blurs into broader over-eager piece maneuvers — other misplaced/centralizing knights (Ne4, Na5, Ng4, Nh5) that hang or get trapped, plus a few non-knight chasing/developing moves (g4, Ba4, Bd6) that lose material.

432.label: Top: a materially-safe slow king/pawn move in a rook endgame squanders the one tempo-gaining rook activation (often a check, intermezzo, or deflection) needed to win or hold; medium broadens to king misdirection across endgames generally — wrong-way king marches, failed blockades, and even walking into mate or hanging a piece.

436.label: Top: in a 100%-lost endgame the king marches the wrong way (toward an enemy pawn it can't catch instead of own counterplay), losing only tempo but blowing the resistance; medium broadens to king moves that additionally step onto squares allowing promotion-with-check or a forced mating net, plus the occasional missed defensive capture.

434.label: Top boards are queen reposition/retreat moves that overlook a decisive forcing capture combination (Qxd1+/Qxf1+/Bxh7+-type back-rank or file tactic); medium blurs to any piece reposition (rook check, knight centralization, queen blocking own rook) that forfeits a faster mate or a clear positional/material edge — direction is mostly 'missed win' but a few peaks instead outright hang material.

438.label: At the peak the player throws away a clearly winning position by a move that directly hangs/ignores free material (e.g., leaving White's queen capturable, then dropping a piece to Bxe5+); at medium activation it broadens to quiet piece-relocating moves (Re3, Nb3) that abandon back-rank/key-square defense and allow a multi-move fork to win material.

444.label: Top: in a won R+P endgame the player inserts a rook check or extra pawn push instead of queening the passed pawn at once (mere tempo loss); medium broadens to king maneuvers (Kc6, e6) that delay promotion without losing material — though a couple of peak boards are genuine blunders (h5 allowing mate, Ra6 dropping forced mate).

442.label: Top: h3/h6 (some a3) 'asking the question' of a pinning bishop on g4/g5, punished by ...Bxf3/...Bxc3 wrecking the pawn structure or by a missed winning tactic; medium broadens to any flank-pawn piece-chase (a6, b5, g5, h4) against a bishop or queen, punished by king-hunts (Qh5+/Qg3+) or central tactics.

446.label: TOP is rock-solid: White/Black plays a quiet developing move (bishop development or castling) instead of recapturing an intruding minor piece (almost always a bishop) in the opening, hanging a full piece; MEDIUM keeps the 'failed to take/address the available enemy capture' core but blurs the trigger — ignoring capture threats (dxc3, exf2+), moving a pinned piece, push-instead-of-capture, even walking into a fork/mate — across more phases.

435.label: Top: advancing one's own passed pawn one square too far onto a permanent blockade square (with sibling king-misplacement in pawn races); medium broadens to committing the rook prematurely to chase or blockade the enemy's passer — in all cases a committal endgame move that sacrifices flexibility/king-activity rather than hanging material.

437.label: Top: an over-ambitious 'active'/centralizing piece advance (Nd5, Qd3, e4, Nf6/Nd4-type) that hangs material to a tactical refutation — knight, check, or capture; medium broadens to any aggressively-placed but loose/undefended piece (or a removed defender) that simply drops material, with the moved piece and material won varying widely.

439.label: At the peak the move 'solves the wrong problem' and hangs material to a forcing refutation (overloaded-defender capture, fork, mate); at medium it blurs to a slow/misplaced piece move (Bf3, Rh6) that throws away a winning advantage on tempo/positional grounds without any immediate material loss.

448.label: Top boards are passive blockading rook moves (sometimes a king move) in already-lost endgames that allow a forced rook trade — or skewer/mating net — into a hopeless king-and-pawn ending; medium blurs to any tempo-wasting passive king/rook (or pawn) move that fails to maximize resistance and accelerates an already-losing position.

447.label: TOP: a king move or removal of the sole defender that walks the player's exposed king into a forced checkmate (position usually already lost); MEDIUM keeps the king-safety/forced-mate core but blurs to also include throwing away equal/drawn positions by skipping the only saving perpetual check and grabbing material while ignoring a mating threat.

440.chip: Hangs piece on greedy grab (often knight fork)
440.label: Top: a knight greedily forks two rooks (Nf2→d1/h1) or king+rook (Nf7) to win the exchange but hangs/traps itself or overlooks a bigger capture; medium broadens to any tempting material/tempo grab — other knight forks plus queen pawn-snatches (Qxb2) and loosening pawn pushes (g3/g4) — punished by a refutation the player ignored.

443.label: Top boards all leave/walk the king onto an open file or diagonal where a decisive, usually mating or queen-winning check sequence follows (Qxd4+, Qb4#, Ng6+, Rxh7+); medium keeps the same king-exposure theme but the checks are less fatal (Rde8+ tempo, Bf5+, Ne3+ fork, Qf5# nets) and it blurs to include a couple of non-king piece relocations that simply hang material (Ne2→Bg4, Nbd2→d4).

450.label: Top boards always fail to grab a free, undefended enemy ROOK (the winning move is a rook capture, usually skipped via a quiet king/pawn move); medium broadens to capturing a lesser piece instead of the rook or, occasionally, missing a hanging QUEEN.

452.label: Top: quiet king moves in winning pawn endgames that pick the wrong square/waste a tempo to convert (though many are actually 0cp-optimal false positives); medium broadens to other tempo-losing quiet moves (rook to wrong file, slow king route) plus a few missed forcing wins/greedy captures that squander a winning advantage, with material never actually hung.

451.label: Top: a king-and-pawn endgame move (misplaced king or wrong move-order) lets a lone enemy passer queen unstopped; medium broadens to any tempo-losing piece move, en passant, or abandoned blockade that loses the pawn race to connected/passed pawns.

458.label: Top: king-and-pawn endgame king moves that take the wrong square (lost opposition, failed blockade/centralization, wasted tempo), mostly in already-decided positions; medium blurs to general endgame king passivity/wrong direction plus occasional rook moves and outright tactical king blunders (fork/skewer).

453.label: Top boards skip a Bxe6/Nxd5 sacrifice that wins via a fork; medium broadens to declining simpler captures of hanging or weak material (Nxg5, bxa3).

445.label: Top: passive defensive or king-flight moves in already-lost positions that allow a forced mate against an exposed king (back-rank/h-file/open-file attacks); medium blurs to any move that merely accelerates an inevitable loss—passed-pawn promotions and drifting endgames—where king safety is no longer the driver, including near-zero-loss non-blunders in dead-lost spots.

455.label: At the peak, a king move in a winning K+P endgame skips the decisive pawn-push/opposition and lets the enemy king blockade in front of the passer, drawing a forced win (often a mate); at medium it blurs into milder king tempo-losses that keep the win, with several flagged moves actually being 0cp non-blunders.

449.label: At the peak an active capture/developing move loses a major piece — often the queen — to a forcing check or fork (Bg4→Bb5+, Rd1→fork, Bd4→Qh4); at medium it blurs to a broader set of tactics (fork, pin, overloaded-defender) that win a piece or the exchange after a natural-looking move.

457.label: Top: an immediate capture wins the enemy QUEEN (usually via knight/bishop) but the player makes a quiet/safe move instead; medium: the target blurs to free rooks/other major pieces or squandered winning tactics, sometimes also hanging own material.

454.label: Top: a wrong/passive king move converts a drawn K+P or piece endgame into a loss, declining the only saving capture (Kxb6, Rxb8) or walking into a skewer/mate net; medium broadens to a pawn move-order error (h4) that hangs a rook and throws a winning endgame to a draw.

460.label: Top boards are uniformly ...Be6 developed into Ng5+, a knight check-fork hitting the exposed f7 king and the just-placed bishop; medium broadens to other opening developing/pawn moves (e.g. g3, Bg4) that likewise hang material to a knight check exploiting the exposed king.

464.label: Top positions almost uniformly miss the Qa4+/Qa5+ queen check that forks the king and a loose b4 bishop to win a piece in the opening; medium blurs to other missed forcing opening shots like the Nb5 knight fork.

459.label: Top: the king walks into a forcing check (Ke7 → Qf7+ or Bg5+ fork) instead of the only defensive move (g6), losing material or getting mated; medium broadens to any move (passive, tempo-losing, or developing) that ignores the position's sole defensive resource and concedes material to a tactical refutation.

456.label: Top: a routine opening fianchetto (Bg7/Bb7) that either drops the bishop into a long-diagonal capture (Bxg7/Bxb7) or ignores a free undefended enemy bishop on h6/a6; medium: broadens to other quiet developing moves (castling, Bb2, Bg2, Be2) and to other undefended minor pieces left hanging (knight on e5, bishop to Qxg4), so the constant 'undefended bishop' target blurs into 'undefended minor piece in the opening'.

465.label: Top boards are king moves in already-lost pawn/passed-pawn endgames where the king heads the wrong way and is simply too slow (often 0cp, near-noise); medium blurs to include genuine wrong-direction king marches that throw an actual draw or win by losing the critical tempo/route.

463.label: Top boards are a developed knight snatching a central pawn (d4/d5/e4/e5) that's instantly won back by a queen recapture or Qa4+/Qd4+ fork; medium broadens the grabber to queens and other pieces (and to wing/rim pawns like a2/b2/c3/h5), punished now by trapping the piece or a king-side attack rather than a clean recapture.

462.label: Top boards play Rxpawn+, sacrificing the rook for a single pawn and throwing away a forced mate after the king recaptures; medium boards run the same rook-for-pawn trade with check but only squander a dominant won rook endgame into a trickier (still winning) pawn endgame.

470.label: Top: a quiet/routine developing or castling move skips a winning king-hunting bishop sacrifice (overwhelmingly Bxf2+, also Bxf7+/Greek-Gift Bxh7+); medium broadens to any missed winning forcing shot — exchange-winning captures (Bxb7/Bxg7), a queen fork (Nxf3), a mating check (Bh3+), or an intermediate move (fxg2) — all materially-safe moves that throw away a winning advantage.

466.label: Top boards push the wrong passer in a won K+P-vs-bishop endgame so it's immediately captured/blockaded (Bxf6, Bxe5), collapsing the win; medium keeps the same 'wrong pawn advanced' core but blurs toward advancing the wrong passer while skipping an instantly winning promotion/discovered-check shot (a4 instead of d2+).

471.label: Top: Black moves the e4-knight off its outpost (Ne4-f6, or grabs with Nxf2), hanging the e5 pawn to the Nxe5 break; medium broadens to other early moves like b3 that instead leave White's own e5 knight hanging to a tactic (Bd4 fork) — constant = an opening move exposing the e5 point, blurring on which side/piece falls.

477.label: Top: trading the last rook into a clearly lost king-and-pawn endgame (Kx recapture); medium broadens to simplifying into other lost simplified endings (minor-piece/knight/bishop, rook-vs-pawns) and capturing the wrong piece while allowing a pawn to promote.

461.label: Top boards are heterogeneous tactical oversights all hinging on a forcing check — missed zwischenzug 22.g6+, allowed mate 23...Qg4#, greedy Kxd4 into c3+/Qg4+/Rd1+, b4 dropping to Qa1+, plus a non-check deflection (Bxd5) — i.e. a balanced-middlegame move ignores a decisive checking refutation; the lone medium board narrows to exactly the greedy king grab Kxd4 walking into a forced mating run of checks.

476.label: Top: in a drawn knight endgame the player skips a free queen capture (Nxb6/Nxh5) by making a king move; medium broadens to missing the single winning move in a pure pawn endgame (Kxb6/h4).

467.label: At the peak the player almost always hangs own material—a quiet king/pawn/piece move (e.g. Kh1) drops a piece to a fork or simple capture instead of the forcing capture that was best; at medium it blurs to materially-safe moves that simply decline the winning capture/tactic, throwing away a clear win (even a forced mate).

478.label: Top boards hang a major piece (usually a rook) after relocating it to an exposed/duty-abandoning square, exploited by a forcing check; medium blurs to abandoning a central defender (e.g. bishop off d4) and dropping a pawn with no check involved.

481.chip: Passive rook move (broadens to any piece)
481.label: Top: a passive/retreating rook move that abandons activity or initiative (often defending a pawn or trading into a lost endgame instead of staying active); medium: same 'chose the passive/slow square' error but blurs to any piece — knight grabs, slow pawn pushes, passive king/queen moves that forfeit the initiative or a sharper winning line.

468.label: At the peak, decisive king-safety errors in forced-mate situations (king walking into mate like Kd2/Bd2, or even abandoning one's own mating net with Qg2); at medium it blurs to king relocations/queenside castling (Kg3, O-O-O) that expose the king and concede material rather than forcing immediate mate.

480.label: At the peak the player captures with the queen (Qx…) to liquidate into a trade that throws away a winning kingside attack or dynamic edge; at medium the pattern blurs to queen trades that walk into a lost/inferior endgame (king activity, bad-bishop, pawn endings), with a minority outright hanging the queen or trading past a forced mate.

485.label: Top: the player walks the king itself onto a square (e.g. Kh2/Kg2/Kf1/Kd6) that invites a decisive check (Qe5+, Bf4+, Qf3+, Qxe5+), losing material or getting mated, usually with the saving 'challenge the invading queen' move ignored; medium broadens beyond king-walks to any move that exposes the king — bishop/rook abandoning a defensive square or diagonal, or a knight vacating a check-blocker — leading to the same kind of refuting check that wins material or forces mate.

483.label: Top: in a critical position demanding a precise/forcing move the player instead chooses a slow or weakening move (Ra5 too slow, f6 opening the diagonal, Nd7 abandoning defense, Kh4 skipping Qe8+, Ke6 walking into a skewer), throwing away a winning or equal eval; medium narrows to flank pawn pushes (h4, a4) that waste a key defensive/attacking tempo and hand the opponent counterplay.

484.label: Top: in a losing pawn/passed-pawn endgame a passive king or pawn move skips the one saving capture—classically Kxe6 grabbing the bishop that shepherds a passer; medium blurs to any missed capture/passive move that lets a passer queen, plus borderline non-blunders and own-piece hangs.

472.label: Top boards punish a quiet, non-forcing piece move that ignores the position's tactical demand and hangs material to a forced refutation; medium boards broaden to similar quiet moves that surrender a winning advantage through positional, structural, or trade concessions rather than outright material.

474.label: Top boards all squander a SHORT forced mate (mate-in-1 to mate-in-4), almost always by hanging the player's own queen/major piece on a capturable square (e.g. Kg6 leaving Qc7, Qf4+ into Rxf4, Qd3+ into Kxd3); medium boards broaden to abandoning LONGER forced mates (mate-in-8 to mate-in-19) via materially-safe but losing-the-win moves — tempo wasters, greedy pawn/piece grabs, or simply playing a non-mating move — so the forced win evaporates without necessarily hanging material, blurring the direction from 'Hangs queen' (peak) to 'Missed mate' (medium).

473.label: Top: from a winning position a quiet/repositioning move misses a decisive winning capture or check (free piece, queen, or forced mate); medium broadens to near-equal positions where a natural-looking move instead hangs material by walking into a fork, pin, or mating sacrifice.

488.label: Top: a pawn-grab or misplaced king/passive piece abandons containment of an enemy passed pawn, which queens unstoppably; medium keeps the 'neglect the urgent defense for a small gain' theme but the punishment blurs into forks, back-rank mates, king-safety nets and promotions.

491.label: At the peak the move is an underpromotion (bishop/knight/rook) that throws away a won pawn/promotion endgame or the fastest mate; at medium it blurs into any winning-endgame king/pawn move (e.g. grabbing a pawn instead of Rh8#) that skips the forced mate or win, with material itself never hung.

487.label: Top: a bishop capture/move leaves Black's own major piece hanging on an open line (e.g., Bxd3 → Rxe7 wins the queen); medium blurs to king walks onto exposed files/ranks (Kf5, Kd3, Kg8) that allow rook checks (Rf7+, Rd8+, Ra3+) winning minor pieces or pawns — but the set also includes pure positional/tempo errors, so the unifying thread is only 'self-exposing move loses material'.

486.label: Top: a knight check that hangs the piece outright or abandons a dominant outpost (king walks to a better square); medium broadens to vanity checks that merely cost tempo/initiative, plus a pawn check and one squandered forced mate.

492.chip: Hangs rook liquidating won endgame (pawn recapture)
492.label: Top: a rook capture (Rxb7, Rxg6) gets recaptured by a pawn WITH CHECK, sacrificing the rook to liquidate a won endgame into a dead draw; medium broadens to rook trades/forcing captures (Rxb2+) and pawn pushes that simplify into a lost or drawn king-and-pawn endgame rather than a clean material hang.

479.label: Top fires on quiet queen/king relocations (and a missed free capture: Kxf5, en passant) in near-equal/drawn spots that forfeit a win or hang material to a forcing refutation; medium broadens to any passive retreat or tempo-waste — knight, rook, bishop, pawn — including king-safety lapses and back-rank mates.

494.label: Top is razor-sharp: the unsound Bxf2+ bishop sacrifice (bishop given for a pawn-plus-check) that throws away a winning opening; medium blurs into other tempting forcing moves — checks, captures, retreats — that squander a won/equal position when one precise move was required.

497.label: Top: a bishop placed on/left on the passer's promotion square hangs directly to the enemy KING (Kxg7/Kxa1/Kxa8), throwing away a won/drawn pawn endgame; medium broadens to the blockading bishop being lost to a rook (Rxg8) or simply mis-placed away from the promotion diagonal, but always an endgame where the side fails to keep its piece controlling the enemy passed pawn's queening square.

502.label: Top: textbook unsound Bxf7+/Bxf2+ bishop sacrifices that drop a full piece for one pawn with no real attacking follow-up; medium keeps the same 'sac a bishop near the king' theme but broadens beyond f7/f2 to Greek-gift Bxh7+/Bxh2+ and even simply leaving an offered bishop hanging.

482.label: At the peak the player makes a tempting knight grab/check (Nxh7, Nxe5, Nxf6+) instead of a clean exchange-winning capture, and at medium this blurs to winning the exchange via an overloaded defender (Bxg6 instead of Nxf6+); genuinely mixed, since several top boards outright HANG material (queen, mate, bishop) rather than merely skip a win.

489.label: Top: varied endgame king/defensive moves that surrender a win or draw by inviting a forced check (peak Re7 self-blocking into perpetual, plus Kf8 walking into Ng6+); medium tightens to the king retreat to f8 that hands over the Ng6+ knight fork and loses the rook.

498.label: Top boards are missed forced checkmates (back-rank/king-safety) thrown away by a quiet or greedy non-check; medium blurs to any forcing-tactic failure — missed material-winning checks/forks but also moves that hang own pieces or allow the opponent's mate.

503.label: Top boards are uniformly voluntary queen trades (Qxd8/Qxd1-type captures into a swap) that squander a winning advantage or pass up free material/a winning tactic; medium broadens to other premature simplifying captures — rook trades, wrong-move-order swaps, and grabbing material — that likewise skip a stronger winning continuation.

495.label: At the peak the constant is a kingside pawn advance (e4/f4) in an already-worse position that shatters the king's shelter and forces mate; at medium it blurs to other ambitious, non-forcing pawn/piece moves that skip the only defensive try and instead hang material or squander the edge rather than allowing outright mate.

507.label: Top: a defender-removing move (often a greedy capture like Rxc6/Rxa6/Rxd2) abandons the sole back-rank guard and walks into a forced back-rank checkmate; medium: the same king-safety neglect broadens to general mating attacks (Qg7#, Qf7+, Rh8#, Nf4 nets) from weakened king cover, with a couple of cases blurring into mere material/tactical loss rather than mate.

508.label: Top is uniformly missing the Bxf7+ bishop sacrifice (→Ne5+/Ng5+ knight fork) in winning opening positions, where White instead plays a routine developing move (O-O, h3, Nc3, Bb3, Bg5, Be3); medium blurs to any missed concrete tactic — preferring a natural developing/castling move over a winning shot — and occasionally tips into actually hanging material (Ne5, Bb7→f3, f3→-99), making the direction mixed.

490.label: Top: king moves that march into a decisive attack or checks (king-safety blunders, sometimes mate) plus over-centralized pieces that get forked/won; medium broadens to active rook/pawn/queen moves that abandon a defender or weaken the king, conceding a winning tactic.

504.label: Top: a king move walks directly into a knight fork or forced mating check, hanging material/king; medium broadens to any king-exposing move (incl. a non-king piece) that loses material to a check-fork.

493.label: Top: rook-endgame errors—trading or shifting the rook off its blockading/defensive duty so a passed pawn queens (or the rook hangs); medium broadens to middlegame defensive lapses where a piece quits its post, letting the queen invade or force perpetual.

510.label: Top boards are uniformly a missed Bxg7/Bxg2 that wins the exchange by snatching the undefended fianchetto pawn and trapping the corner rook on the open long diagonal; medium keeps the long-diagonal/fianchetto-capture motif but broadens the capturing piece and target (Qxg7, Qxb7, Qxb2, Bxb7, Bxb2) with a few cases bleeding into hung/trapped own pieces.

509.label: Top: an opening move vacates c7 (or undefends f7), hanging material to a Nxc7+/Nxf7 outpost knight fork; medium broadens to other moves that weaken a key square (f2, c2, h2, f7) and hang material to forks, sacrifices, or king attacks.

511.label: Top: own queen left undefended/on an open line (usually by playing an unrelated knight or developing move, or ignoring queen tension) and snapped off the next move; medium: blurs to a minor piece — most often a bishop that captured on d4 — lost to a queen recapture, plus a few positional/trade lapses that just surrender the advantage.

506.label: At the peak the player moves a major piece (queen/rook) off defense and is hit by a decisive forcing check — back-rank mate or a queen/material-winning fork; at medium it blurs into any move that ignores the opponent's forcing reply (tempo hit on the queen, knight fork, discovered check, simple recapture) and drops the advantage, with a few cases being a missed own forcing shot.

496.label: At the peak the move is a decisive king-safety collapse where an active-looking advance/recapture allows mate or a winning king attack (Nxf7→Qxh7#, dxc3→Qd5+); at medium it blurs to ordinary middlegame material loss from the same overextension (knight trapped on d4, dropped g5 pawn, overloaded defender losing a piece), with a few outlier purely-positional errors.

499.label: Top: a committal king-side/structural pawn push that loosens the king and is refuted by a winning rook or pawn check (Rg3+/Rh3+/e5+) in the endgame; medium: blurs to any premature pawn push (or occasional piece move) that ignores the critical demand—passed-pawn race, central tension, tempo—conceding structure or material in middlegames too.
